description: Add a project to the room, change its sources or roster, or archive it; writes project.yaml, the memory scaffold, and the automation checklist
Write and post the morning brief across every active project
Alert new fires, take in comms, apply Slack thread replies, and send the grouped digest
Route new client email and Slack messages into the right project's inbox, or to Unsorted
Run a project's daily stand-up and hand Maestro an honest cue sheet
Turn inbox items, source events, and polled changes into routed, owned work for the squad
Close a project's day, curate the squad's memory, and set up tomorrow's stand-up
Draft a project's weekly stakeholder update and raise a hand to post it
Post what the operator approved for a project, and have the squad post theirs
Show what needs the operator across the room: asks, approvals, and fires
Gather new feedback into the evidence ledger and rank themes by people, channels, and recency
Turn a stakeholder request into the problem underneath, its evidence, its goal, and questions to send back
One-page brief for a theme: problem, evidence and strength, goal, assumptions, directions, what to validate
Plan the cheapest tests for an opportunity's riskiest assumptions, with results that would change the decision
Turn an opportunity, brief, or request into an epic and ready, testable stories; one approval creates them in Jira
Check Jira stories against the Definition of Ready and draft suggested acceptance criteria
Prepare the next refinement: which stories, in what order, and the questions each needs answered
Review a story's designs for every state it needs and for accessibility
Walk a flow and flag inconsistent words, patterns, and dead ends
Map stories to their frames for a sprint or epic: ready, in progress, or no design
Collect open designer questions, answer what sources settle, and route the rest
Challenge a story and write scenarios that trace every acceptance criterion, including the breaks
Check a pull request's tests and CI results against its story's acceptance criteria
Reproduce a bug, rate severity by the team's rubric, find duplicates and the likely change
Give a release a go, go-with-risks, or no-go verdict from the evidence
Explain a pull request in plain language and flag gaps between the change and its story
Report added, removed, and major-bumped dependencies and the work a change blocks or relies on
Answer an engineer's question from the sources, or route it as a precise question to its owner
Plain-language digest of what merged, grouped by story, with untracked and risky changes
Record a decision with who, when, why, and what it supersedes, and list the documents that now disagree
Compare docs, tickets, designs, and code on one subject and report every disagreement
Find avoided terms, propose missing glossary entries, and keep the glossary sound
Draft a PRD change section by section after a decision or story change
Draft release notes per audience from what actually shipped
